summary: Ruth is Henry Bell's illegitimate daughter. Her mother Doris Calder raised her on the south lane. The Bell family paid Doris to disappear. Ruth returned to this village forty years later under her married name.

At 18:00 Ruth confronted Marcus with the birth certificate. He acknowledged the relationship but refused to alter the will further. He told her to contest — but contested wills take years, and she knew he would fight it. She decided on the walk home.

Ruth spent the summer reading about cardiac glycosides. She grew the foxglove for two seasons. She had her method ready before the confrontation — she had been planning this since Marcus's last health scare, when she realised time was running out.

Ruth's cover: she was home all evening gardening and went to bed by nine. She had no relationship with Marcus beyond the post. She presents as the reliable, helpful postwoman — utterly without motive.

Marcus knew Ruth was his half-sister. He acknowledged it privately but could not face a public contest. His will note — 'if R. contests, she may have legal standing' — was a private admission to Whittle, not an invitation.

Isabella went to confront Marcus about the will. He would not change it. She left at 20:00 in a rage. She considered contesting but went home and drank wine instead. She had nothing to do with his death.

Elias vaguely remembers the village rumour — Henry Bell and a woman on the south lane. A daughter sent away. He never connected it to Ruth Calder. When prompted, he thinks the daughter's name was Ruth.
Nadia can identify the cocoa residue and foxglove evidence as consistent with digitalis poisoning. She is disturbed — she trusted Marcus's death was natural. She provides the medical framework.

Ruth has held a key to Marcus's house for years — he gave it to her himself for the registered post, and never thought about it again. She let herself in on the evening of the 14th while he was in his study, and put the foxglove extract into the cocoa tin he would use at nine o'clock, the way he did every night of his life.

Nadia helped Marcus word the clinic's share of his estate years ago and had quietly built the clinic's plans around it. She learned it had been struck out on the morning after he died, and she is painfully aware of how that looks alongside her knowing exactly what killed him.
Nadia was called out at 20:40 to a confinement at Bracken Farm, six miles out, and did not return until after one.
